source.page_or_item: 44 FR 43248, PDF page 18, sections 1-204, 1-301, 1-303, signature
source.read_method: complete official extract read; no image verification claimed
quoted_parts:
1-204. Each Council shall attempt to identify significant problems with Federal 
policies and actions and, if such problems cannot be resolved in the Region, 
refer such problems to the appropriate agencies and the Interagency Coordi­
nating Council.

1-301. The Interagency Coordinating Council, in conjunction with the Office of 
Management and Budget shall, consistent with the objectives and priorities 
established by the President, establish policy with respect to Federal Regional 
Council matters, provide guidance to the Councils, respond to their initiatives 
and seek to resolve policy issues referred to it by the Councils. The Inter­
agency Coordinating Council shall also provide policy guidance to the Federal 
Cochairmen of the Regional Action Planning Commissions on intergovernmen­
tal matters pertaining to activities undertaken by the Federal Regional Coun­
cils.

1-303. Each Agency represented on a Council shall provide, to the extent 
permitted by law, appropriate staff for common or joint interagency task 
forces as requested by the Federal Regional Council Chairman or by the 
Interagency Coordinating Council.

THE WHITE HOUSE, 
J u ly  20, 1979.

later_events.mechanism: Expressly revokes EO 12149 and puts regional-council policy/oversight in OMB; removes the independently added ICC regional-council branch. No express or necessary extinguishment of the broader original EO 12075 commands.

source.page_or_item: 46 FR 38330, PDF page 10, sections 3 and 4 and signature
source.read_method: complete official extract read; no image verification claimed
quoted_parts:
Sec. 3. O v e rs ig h t
(a) The Office of M anagem ent and Budget will provide policy guidance to the  
Councils in consultation with the W hite House Office of Policy Development;  
establish policy with respect to Federal Regional Council procedural matters;  
respond to Council initiatives; seek to resolve policy issues referred to it by  
the Councils; coordinate Federal Regional Council activities relating to State  
and local governments with the W hite House Office of Intergovernmental  
Affairs; and, coordinate Council activities relating to specific programmatic  
areas with the appropriate Federal agencies.
(b) The Office of M anagem ent and Budget shall provide direction for, and  
oversight of, the implementation by the Councils of Federal management  
improvement actions and of Federal aid reforms.
Sec. 4. G e n e r a l P ro v is io n s .
(a) Each agency represented on a Council shall provide, to the extent permit­
ted by law, appropriate staff for common or joint interagency activities as  
requested by the Chairm an of the Council.
(b) Executive O rder No. 12149 is revoked.

THE W H ITE HOUSE,  
J u ly  2 2 , 1981.

later_events.mechanism: whole-order revocation of EO 12075 as amended

research_rationale: Version2 corrects the rejected first candidate without changing its frozen files or provisional status. The complete original has twelve numbered operative provisions; its single roster is now split into five contiguous groups, giving sixteen inventory units and isolating HEW and CSA. The Council and its broad functions have no sunset or report-triggered expiry. EO12148 adds FEMA effective July15,1979 under its express section6; it does not end existing roster commands. EO 12149 section 1-204 sends unresolved regional problems to the ICC; section 1-301 assigns ICC/OMB regional-council policy, guidance and referrals, including guidance to Federal Cochairmen; section 1-303 permits ICC requests for joint staff. These are concrete additional duties under EO 12149. EO 12314 section 4(b) expressly revokes that order and section 3 locates regional-council oversight in OMB on July 22, 1981. It neither names EO 12075 nor states that the ICC is abolished. Its narrower regional-council administration is compatible with original 1-201 to 1-204 assistance, coordination and problem-solving across executive agencies and community sectors; 1-205 already preserves EOP clearance/review/decisionmaking. Thus 1981 ends the separately added duties, not every original broad command. General support, working-group power and reporting remain tied to the surviving original Council functions. EO 12407 later revokes EO 12314 on February 22, 1983 without recreating ICC or EO 12149 duties. The HEW lead concerns name/succession after a concrete reorganization, whereas the CSA lead concerns abolition and transfer. Actual statutory texts remain unavailable, so first_end is null only for these two original seat units and savings/search closure is withheld. Fourteen other original units retain August17,1982 under the complete EO12379 section14 revocation and signature. The whole-order end remains that date because independently continuing broad Council commands end then; unresolved seats may have ended earlier but are not asserted to outlast revocation. No 1981 date is mechanically assigned to original commands, and the generic 1982 inactivity preamble supplies no earlier legal date. All legal source readings are held official extracts with official GPO fixity; editorial roster notes are explicitly leads, not originals. Complete acceptance is not requested.
unresolved_material_gaps: Section 1-102(g): actual P.L.96-88 / 20 USC3508(b) reorganization, reference/succession and savings text is not held/read. EO12212 establishes May4,1980 for the Act; the editorial redesignation lead does not establish seat cessation. Preserve first_end null until the original legal effect is resolved.

Section 1-102(l): actual P.L.97-35 abolition/transfer/savings and effective-date text around95Stat516-519 is not held/read. OFR editorial abolition lead is concrete, but neither its exact first-end date nor succession of this Council seat is established.

Overall savings/residuals closure and final adequate later-source-search acceptance remain pending the two narrow statutory roster investigations. Numeric and named-body search work is recorded separately; it is not universal exhaustion.
